text:
In the reproof of chance
Lies the true proof of men.
plain: Adversity is the test. Calm seas prove nothing about a person.

text:
Take but degree away, untune that string,
And hark what discord follows!
plain: Remove order and discipline and everything falls into noise.

text:
And appetite, an universal wolf,
So doubly seconded with will and power,
Must make perforce an universal prey,
And last eat up himself.
plain: Unchecked appetite with power behind it ends up devouring itself.

text:
Thus to persist
In doing wrong extenuates not wrong,
But makes it much more heavy.
plain: Doubling down on a wrong does not shrink it. It makes it heavier.

text:
O theft most base,
That we have stol’n what we do fear to keep!
plain: The worst kind of shame is grabbing something and then being scared to hold it.

text: What’s aught but as ’tis valued?
plain: Things are worth what you decide they are worth.

text: He that is proud eats up himself. Pride is his own glass, his own trumpet, his own chronicle; and whatever praises itself but in the deed devours the deed in the praise.
plain: Pride feeds on itself. Praising your own work eats the work.

text: The amity that wisdom knits not, folly may easily untie.
plain: What wisdom ties together, one foolish move can undo.

text: Blind fear, that seeing reason leads, finds safer footing than blind reason stumbling without fear. To fear the worst oft cures the worse.
plain: Fear that sees clearly beats confidence that sees nothing. Expecting the worst often heads it off.

text: This is the monstruosity in love, lady, that the will is infinite, and the execution confin’d; that the desire is boundless, and the act a slave to limit.
plain: Wanting has no ceiling. What you can actually do always does.

text:
’Tis certain, greatness, once fall’n out with fortune,
Must fall out with men too.
plain: When your luck turns, people turn with it.

text:
Time hath, my lord, a wallet at his back,
Wherein he puts alms for oblivion,
A great-siz’d monster of ingratitudes.
Those scraps are good deeds past, which are devour’d
As fast as they are made, forgot as soon
As done. Perseverance, dear my lord,
Keeps honour bright.
plain: Time forgets what you did yesterday. Only showing up again keeps your name alive.

text:
The welcome ever smiles,
And farewell goes out sighing. O, let not virtue seek
Remuneration for the thing it was;
For beauty, wit,
High birth, vigour of bone, desert in service,
Love, friendship, charity, are subjects all
To envious and calumniating Time.
plain: Everyone greets the new thing and forgets the old. Beauty, wit and even friendship are at time's mercy.

text:
One touch of nature makes the whole world kin—
That all with one consent praise new-born gauds,
Though they are made and moulded of things past,
And give to dust that is a little gilt
More laud than gilt o’er-dusted.
plain: People rush to praise what is shiny and new, even if it is made of old stuff.
The damage you do yourself by sitting out heals worst. Doing nothing is a choice with a price.

text:
My mind is troubled, like a fountain stirr’d;
And I myself see not the bottom of it.
plain: When your mind is churning you cannot see to the bottom of it.

text:
And sometimes we are devils to ourselves,
When we will tempt the frailty of our powers,
Presuming on their changeful potency.
plain: We can be our own devil by testing how strong we really are.

text:
What’s past and what’s to come is strew’d with husks
And formless ruin of oblivion;
plain: The past and the future are rubble. Only this moment is solid.
Judge it at the end. Time settles every argument eventually.

text:
Mine honour keeps the weather of my fate.
Life every man holds dear; but the dear man
Holds honour far more precious dear than life.
plain: Everyone holds life dear, but a man of honour holds his word dearer.

text:
Words, words, mere words, no matter from the heart;
Th’effect doth operate another way.
plain: Words are cheap. What matters is what the heart actually does.

text:
I do not speak of flight, of fear of death,
But dare all imminence that gods and men
Address their dangers in.
plain: Don't let fear of death make your choices.

text:
If music be the food of love, play on,
Give me excess of it; that, surfeiting,
The appetite may sicken and so die.
plain: Overdo what you crave and the craving dies on its own.

text:
So full of shapes is fancy,
That it alone is high fantastical.
plain: Desire changes shape constantly. Nothing it takes in keeps its value for long.

text: Dost thou think, because thou art virtuous, there shall be no more cakes and ale?
plain: Just because you live clean does not mean everyone else has to quit the fun.

text: Better a witty fool than a foolish wit.
plain: Better to be a clever fool than a stupid wise man.

text:
What else may hap, to time I will commit;
Only shape thou thy silence to my wit.
plain: What happens, happens. Leave it to time and keep your mouth shut.

text:
Alas, our frailty is the cause, not we,
For such as we are made of, such we be.
plain: We are made the way we are made. The fault is in the material, not the person.

text:
O time, thou must untangle this, not I,
It is too hard a knot for me t’untie!
plain: Some knots are too tight for you to untie. Let time do it.

text:
Fate, show thy force, ourselves we do not owe.
What is decreed must be; and be this so!
plain: You don't control how it plays out. Face it anyway.

text:
What is love? ’Tis not hereafter,
Present mirth hath present laughter.
What’s to come is still unsure.
In delay there lies no plenty,
Then come kiss me, sweet and twenty.
Youth’s a stuff will not endure.
plain: Enjoy now. The future is uncertain and youth does not last.

text:
She never told her love,
But let concealment, like a worm i’ th’ bud,
Feed on her damask cheek: she pined in thought,
And with a green and yellow melancholy
She sat like patience on a monument,
Smiling at grief.
plain: She never said it and it ate her alive. Silence about what you feel does damage.

text:
But come what may, I do adore thee so,
That danger shall seem sport, and I will go.
plain: Come what may, I love you enough that danger looks like play.

text:
Dexterity so obeying appetite
That what he will he does, and does so much
That proof is call’d impossibility.
plain: When skill and will line up, the thing you do gets called impossible.

text:
A stirring dwarf we do allowance give
Before a sleeping giant.
plain: A small man in motion is worth more than a giant lying down.
